# Story 38 — Live Chat Communication Channel

## Prerequisites

- **CRITICAL — Ticket entity coordination (H-2):** This story **MUST** reuse the `Ticket` entity definition from `tickets/create-ticket` (Plan 30). Do **NOT** define an independent `Ticket` entity. Plan 30 owns the Ticket shape with fields `Id`, `CustomerId`, `Customer` navigation, etc. Plan 38 defines only `ChatSession` and `ChatMessage` as chat-specific entities.
- **CRITICAL — Customer authentication gap (H-9):** This plan assumes a customer role and customer JWT flow that do **not** exist in the backend yet. Roles defined in `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Constants/Roles.cs` are: `Admin`, `Supervisor`, `Manager`, `Agent`. There is no `Roles.Customer` and no `SuperAdmin` role. **This story is blocked until customer authentication is designed and implemented.** Flag this in Done Criteria and escalate to product/architecture before implementation.
- Backend baseline verified: Clean Architecture solution `src/BackEnd/CustomerSupportCRM.sln` with projects **Domain**, **Application**, **Infrastructure**, **API**. EF Core + Identity + JWT already wired.
- Frontend baseline verified: React + Vite + TypeScript + MUI + i18next (`ar`/`en`) + React Query + `AuthContext`.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver a functioning **live-chat** channel where a Customer can start a chat session from the customer-facing UI, and an available Agent can respond in real time from the agent dashboard. Chat messages are persisted and associated with a `Ticket` (created on-demand when the session begins). If no agent is currently available, the customer receives an "offline" acknowledgement and the session is queued as an unassigned open ticket that any agent can later pick up.

**Decisions taken (previously open questions in intake):**

1. **Real-time transport:** ASP.NET Core **SignalR** (already available in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` framework reference; no external broker). Frontend uses `@microsoft/signalr`.
2. **Chat ⇄ Ticket relationship:** every chat session **creates a ticket** on the first customer message (or attaches to an explicitly provided existing ticket id). Chat messages are persisted rows linked to that ticket.
3. **Agent-unavailable fallback:** session is still created, ticket is created in status `Open` and unassigned; the customer receives a system message "No agent is available right now, we have opened a support ticket and an agent will reply shortly." The session stays live; when an agent joins, they see the backlog.

**Out of scope** (per intake): WhatsApp/SMS channels; typing indicators; file attachments in chat; read receipts; email/push notifications on unread messages; chatbot autoresponders.

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour:** the product has no real-time channel; there is no `Ticket` or chat schema in the database (only Identity tables per the single existing migration `InitialIdentitySchema`).

**New behaviour:**

- A customer authenticated via JWT can `POST /api/chat/sessions` to open a chat session; the API creates a `Ticket` (status `Open`, source `LiveChat`, no assignee), a `ChatSession` bound to it, and returns the session id + ticket id. **See Prerequisites: customer auth flow does not exist yet.**
- The customer connects to the SignalR hub `/hubs/chat` and calls `JoinSession(sessionId)` then `SendMessage(sessionId, text)`.
- Agents (role `Agent`, `Supervisor`, or `Admin`) connect to the same hub and are subscribed by role group; unassigned sessions broadcast to the `agents-lobby` group; once an agent calls `AssignToMe(sessionId)`, the ticket is assigned and future messages route to the session group only.
- Every hub message is persisted as `ChatMessage` (senderUserId, sessionId, ticketId, text, sentAtUtc) before being echoed to the group, so history survives reload.
- If no agent is in the `agents-lobby` group at session start, the API immediately posts a system `ChatMessage` with a localized “no agent available” body; the ticket remains open and unassigned.

- **Create file:** `src/FrontEnd/src/features/chat/api/chatClient.ts`:

```ts
import { HubConnectionBuilder, LogLevel } from '@microsoft/signalr';
import { getAccessToken } from '@/lib/auth/tokenStorage';

export function buildChatConnection(baseUrl: string) {
  return new HubConnectionBuilder()
    .withUrl(`${baseUrl}/hubs/chat`, { accessTokenFactory: () => getAccessToken() ?? '' })
    .withAutomaticReconnect()
    .configureLogging(LogLevel.Warning)
    .build();
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty message body** → server-side `PostChatMessageCommandValidator` rejects with 400; frontend disables the Send button until input has non-whitespace characters. Enforcement: `Application/Features/Chat/Commands/PostChatMessage/Validator.cs` and the send-button `disabled` prop.
- **Message body over 4000 chars** → validator trims/rejects; UI enforces `maxLength={4000}` and shows an inline warning.
- **Unicode / RTL text (Arabic)** → messages stored as `nvarchar`; `ChatMessage.Body` configured as `IsUnicode(true)`. Chat bubble component uses the app-wide direction from `useDirection.ts`; verify mixed LTR/RTL rendering with a right-aligned bubble in `ar`.
- **Customer opens a second session while one is already open for the same ticket** → `ChatSessionConfiguration` sets a unique index on `TicketId` for `EndedAtUtc IS NULL`; API returns the existing open session instead of creating a duplicate. Enforcement: `StartChatSessionCommandHandler`.
- **Agent disconnects mid-conversation** → SignalR `OnDisconnectedAsync` does **not** unassign the ticket; the ticket keeps its assignee. Reconnect is handled by `withAutomaticReconnect()` on the client. History reload on reconnect via `GET .../messages`.
- **Customer refreshes the page** → new hub connection, then `JoinSession(existingSessionId)` (read from localStorage keyed by user id) and re-fetch messages.
- **Two agents race to `AssignToMe`** → handler uses `UPDATE ... WHERE AssignedAgentUserId IS NULL` (optimistic in a single SaveChanges) and returns 409 to the loser; the loser’s UI shows a toast and refreshes the queue.
- **JWT expired mid-session** → `apiClient.ts` refresh flow handles REST; for the hub, `accessTokenFactory` runs on every reconnect. Enforcement: `chatClient.ts` + existing `tokenStorage.ts`.
- **No agent online at session start** → `StartChatSessionCommandHandler` inserts a system `ChatMessage` with key `Chat.NoAgentAvailable` (localized). Enforcement documented above.
- **Cross-origin WebSocket blocked** → verify CORS allows credentials; test in `AllowedOrigins` config for `appsettings.Development.json`.
- **Message ordering under retries** → server assigns `SentAtUtc = DateTime.UtcNow` at handler entry; client sorts by `SentAtUtc` ascending, breaking ties by `Id` (Guid v7 preferred, but any Guid is acceptable for MVP).
- **Deleting a user with historical messages** → `ChatMessage.SenderUserId` uses `OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.NoAction)` so history is preserved as an orphan display name “Deleted user”.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** run `dotnet ef database update AddChatAndTicketSchema` from `src/BackEnd`.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update 20260901090336_InitialIdentitySchema` (previous migration) then `dotnet ef migrations remove`.
- **Half-applied risk:** if the migration is applied but code deploy fails, existing endpoints are unaffected (only new tables were added). If code is deployed but migration is not applied, calls to `POST /api/chat/sessions` will throw a runtime SQL error; the CI pipeline must apply migrations **before** rolling out the API.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** from `src/BackEnd`, run `dotnet build CustomerSupportCRM.sln`.
2. **Migration applies:** from `src/BackEnd`, run `dotnet ef database update --project src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure --startup-project src/CustomerSupportCRM.API`.
3. **Backend tests:** from `src/BackEnd`, run `dotnet test`.
4. **Backend runs:** from `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API`, run `dotnet run`; hit `GET /health` (200), `POST /api/chat/sessions` with a customer JWT (201), and open a WebSocket to `/hubs/chat?access_token=…`.
5. **Frontend installs:** from `src/FrontEnd`, run `npm install` then `npm run lint` and `npm run build`.
6. **Frontend runs:** from `src/FrontEnd`, run `npm run dev`; log in as a customer, open `/chat`, send a message; in a second browser session log in as an agent, open `/agent/chats`, click the session, reply.
7. **Regression:** existing `GET /health` still returns 200; existing auth flows (login, JWT bearer) still work; no changes to Identity tables in the new migration.
